operations.evidence: The release covers police powers under terrorism and subsequent legislation in Great Britain up to 31 March 2026.
The release does not provide parcel-level or exact-location risk evidence.
The statistics draw on administrative sources that are updated as cases progress and may be revised in future releases.
Current outcomes must not be treated as final while cases remain open.
There were 3,061 arrests for terrorism-related activity in the year ending 31 March 2026.
The total was strongly affected by a specific proscription and is not a stable local-risk baseline.
Of the 3,061 arrests, 2,819 were linked to supporting Palestine Action after proscription on 5 July 2025.
The linked category must be separated from other terrorism-related arrests for comparison.
Excluding Palestine Action-linked arrests, there were 242 arrests, 1.7% more than the previous year.
The small change must not be confused with the increase in the all-arrest total.
There were 44 non-Palestine-Action arrests in January to March 2026, 32% fewer than the previous quarter.
Quarterly volatility does not establish a persistent local trend.
At the data-provision date, 551 arrests had resulted in a charge.
The charge rate can change as unresolved cases progress.
Forty-one people aged 17 and under were arrested in the year ending March 2026.
Age-group counts do not support prediction about an individual or parcel.
Case outcomes were based on the latest recorded position supplied by CTPHQ on 5 May 2026.
Later releases may show different outcomes for the same arrest cohort.
Seventy-two persons were tried for terrorism-related offences in the year ending March 2026.
Trial-date statistics are not directly comparable with arrest-cohort statistics.
There were 273 persons in custody for terrorism and terrorism-connected offences at 31 March 2026.
The custody snapshot is a national stock measure, not a local incident measure.
The Metropolitan Police Service carried out 98 section 43 stop and searches in the year ending March 2026.
This MPS count must not be generalised to every police force or parcel.
Other police forces in England and Wales reported 108 section 43 searches for the first time as statistics in development.
The new coverage creates a comparability break with earlier MPS-only data.
Sixteen arrests resulted from MPS section 43 stop and searches in the year ending March 2026.
The arrest rate is based on small counts and is not a parcel-risk probability.
Twenty-two arrests resulted from section 43 searches by other police forces in England and Wales.
These statistics are in development and require explicit quality qualification.
There were 14 instances in January to March 2026 where access to a solicitor was delayed.
The count is an operational-process measure, not a crime-prevalence measure.
Ethnic appearance is recorded by the arresting officer and uses the ONS 18+1 classification.
Officer-observed ethnicity is not equivalent to self-defined ethnicity.
Of 2,819 linked arrests, 484 were charged, 36 released without charge, 12 had alternative action and 2,287 were bailed or released under investigation.
Open outcomes must not be summed as final disposals.
Forty arrests were under section 41 of TACT 2000 and 3,021 were under other legislation.
Other legislation includes non-terrorism statutes, so statute and terrorism-related classification are distinct.
Where a person is charged with multiple offences at the same time, the statistics count the most serious offence.
Charge statistics count people under a principal-offence rule, not every charge laid.
